newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Sao Paulo to see larger 1997/98 orange crop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Sao Paulo to see larger 1997/98 orange crop.

text.p: The 1997/98 orange crop in the Brazilian state of Sao Paulo is likely to be larger than the 1996/97 harvest, a state agronomist said.

"Based on flowerings which were excellent, the crop should be between 375 million and 380 million (40.8 kg) boxes against 350 million last year," said Antonio Ambrosio, director of the Sao Paulo Institute of Agricultural Economics.
The institute should have another estimate at the beginning of April, he added.
Ambrosio said based on the age and the number of trees, the tendency is also for the crop to grow to around 390 million boxes by 1999.
But much will depend on other factors such as whether farmers with low productivity or who live a long way from processing plants will continue in the sector, he added.
Ambrosio estimated that around 100 million boxes from this year's harvest will be directed into the domestic market leaving around 270 million for processing.
"It will be around the same level as last year. That is also a question of policy," Ambrosio said.
Brazil's Citrus Exporters Association has estimated the 1996/97 crop at 352 million boxes, of which 247 million boxes were processed.

The harvest this year should begin at the end of May, earlier than usual, because of the abundant rains over the past few months, said Leonardo Kossoy, president of the Association of Citrus Growers of Sao Paulo State (Aciesp).
The humid conditions have helped the spread of certain pests but these have not outweighed the advantages of the rains.
Prices being offered by processors are better than last year, Kossoy said.

Up to 60 percent of producers last year signed two to three-year contracts with processors but of the 30-40 percent left, very few have signed agreements for this year because of the large variety of offers, he added.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
